context.paragraph: runtime/capture.py#Observer#trace sets opcode tracing on each target-frame event, retaining line callbacks to enable instruction instrumentation in this revision. The recording omits line events themselves. Browser execution emits each observed event immediately and suspends at opcode boundaries until the UI grants a permit. Each opcode snapshot describes state before that instruction executes. Call, return, exception, and unwind events carry locals and output but do not claim an opcode stack snapshot.

otherReferences.paragraph: runtime/capture.py#Observer#trace records coroutine yield and re-entry as suspend and resume, retaining the same frame identity across awaits. Replay updates the resumed frame's current caller, rather than treating suspension as completion or resumption as a new activation. Native, WASM, and Chrome tests exercise async sleep and output, with native/WASM assertions for stable suspension/resumption identity.

otherReferences.paragraph: Live Run uses JSPI when available and a shared-memory worker gate otherwise. web/worker.mjs registers an Emscripten filesystem device. runtime/capture.py#Observer#trace emits the pre-instruction snapshot, then reads one permit byte. With JSPI, an asynchronous read suspends the WASM stack until the UI resolves it. Without JSPI, the read blocks only the worker using Atomics.wait; the main thread writes a shared permit and notifies it. An atomic compare/exchange consumes each permit, including a permit delivered before the worker begins waiting. Both paths advance the same interpreter and never pre-capture a run.
